prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer looks down at a partially built brick-and-mortar wall (mid-grey, roughly 0.4–0.6 metres below) and a grey concrete floor/ground surface further below (darker grey, roughly 1.2–1.5 metres away), with a dark drop-off on the far right edge. The brightest, nearest region (0.15–0.4 metres) is the camera wearer's own left arm in a pink sleeve extending from the bottom-left toward the upper-center to hold the left end of an upper brick within arm's reach, while a second person's right hand (or the wearer's right hand/coworker's hand) enters from the right edge at roughly 0.5–0.6 metres distance, about 0.15–0.2 metres to the right of the left hand on the same brick. Across the 5 frames, the left sleeve and forearm shift slightly upward and closer (brightening at the bottom-left), the upper brick is adjusted slightly upward/rightward on the wall course, and in frame 5 the right hand shifts right as a bamboo/wooden pole at the bottom-right becomes more visible just below the right bricks. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground brick course and outstretched arm from the recessed concrete slab below despite harsh diagonal shadows and similar grey mortar/concrete tones, and it captures the slight elevation of the top right brick above the course below it. However, the map is unreliable along the thin metal pins and string line on the left (which nearly vanish into the background depth) and in the deep shadow on the far right, which is rendered as pitch-black infinite depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a single 'person' mask (pink) corresponding to the camera wearer's left forearm, pink shirt sleeve, and hand reaching from the bottom-left corner to the upper-center of the frame across all 5 frames, at roughly 0.15–0.5 metres from the camera. Across the 5 frames, this mask tracks the arm's slight upward and rightward reach as the hand grasps the left edge of the top brick, while all other body parts of the wearer and any other person remain out of view or unsegmented. The map completely fails to segment the second hand touching the right side of the top brick (at ~0.5–0.6 metres) as well as all non-person objects, including the bricks, wet mortar, string line, nails, and concrete background. Furthermore, the segmentation is unreliable on the left side in frames 1–2 where it falsely bleeds into the red brick and grey mortar course, and in frames 4–5 where it produces small false-positive 'person' patches on the bamboo/wooden pole at the bottom-right. Unlike RGB, it provides a clean binary contour of the wearer's reaching left arm and sleeve in the middle frames, but offers no spatial information about the wall geometry or the second hand.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons despite the clear presence of two hands within 0.4–0.6 metres in the RGB strip. In the RGB context, the camera wearer's head-mounted viewpoint is oriented sharply downward toward the top of the brick wall, with the wearer's torso and head out of view behind the camera and only the left forearm/hand (entering from bottom-left) and a right hand (entering from middle-right, spaced ~0.15–0.2 metres apart on the same brick) visible within arm's reach. As the frames progress from left to right, the left hand maintains a top-down pinch grip on the left end of the brick while the right hand rests flat against its top/front face and shifts slightly right in frame 5, partially occluding the right side of that brick while the left forearm occludes the mortar bed beneath it. Because the pose estimator requires fuller body context or less extreme top-down foreshortening and mortar dust coating on the skin, the pose map is entirely unreliable here and provides no spatial information beyond what must be read directly from the RGB frames.
